# Metric Widget

**Figma:** Metric-Card (Type: KPI · Sparkline · Spark-Bars · Goal-Progress · Comparison · Category-Bar · Hero), Primitives/Metric/Metric-Inline/*, .Primitives/Metrics/Metric-Trend (page 595:54968)  
**Import:** `import { Metric, MetricCard, MetricTrend } from "@zen-ds/react";`

Show one key number with its label, an identifying icon and how it changed; a MetricCard type adds the small picture behind it (a trend line, recent bars, a goal, a split or a comparison).

## Use it for
- Dashboard KPI tiles (MetricCard).
- Summary rows above tables or charts (Metric Small/Medium inline).
- A single highlighted figure in a card or panel.
- A KPI and the shape of its last periods → MetricCard type="sparkline" (a line) or "spark-bars" (bars, the current one highlighted).
- A number toward its goal → MetricCard type="goal-progress".
- Two to four related numbers under one title (invoiced, collected, overdue) → MetricCard type="comparison".
- A total and its 2–7 parts → MetricCard type="category-bar".
- The one number a dashboard leads with → MetricCard type="hero" (Brand Pale; theme="solid" for the dark widget) with a footer button.

## Use something else for
- A series people read point by point (axes, a value per period) → LineChart or BarChart in a ChartCard; a sparkline only shows the shape.
- Many comparable numbers → Table.
- Progress of a task, an upload or a quota → ProgressBar.
- More than 7 parts of a total → DonutChart, BarList or a Table.
- More than one hero in a row → one hero, the rest plain MetricCards.

| Figma | Prop | Values / notes |

| Icon colour | `iconTheme · iconBackground · iconEmoji` | any Dock-Icon theme (Neutral default) · Subtle / Solid · Theme=Emoji |
| Type | `MetricCard type` | kpi (default: Icon-Highlight XLarge) · sparkline · spark-bars · goal-progress · category-bar (Title-Highlight Large) · comparison (Heading/Subheading title + Small columns) · hero (Title-Highlight XLarge); Figma Metric-Card Type |
| Series | `series · seriesLabel · format` | sparkline · spark-bars · hero: numbers oldest first, the last the current period; 64px line (Border/Accent/Solid over an Accent/Solid → Subtle area at 16%) · 48px bars (Chart Sector/Primary, the last Sector/Secondary) · 64px neutral line (hero); an accessible summary ("Trend over 12 periods: from … to …, low …, high …") |
| Goal | `goal {value, target, label?, valueLabel?}` | goal-progress: a stacked Accent ProgressBar, "of {target} goal" and the share (past 100% too) |
| Comparison | `comparison[] {id, label, value, trend?}` | 2–4 columns Spacing/Gap/Medium apart, a Border/Neutral/Subtle rule before each but the first; stacked under 440px |
| Categories | `categories[] {id, label, value, color?}` | category-bar: a 12px bar of shares in the chart palette, then a row per category (Caption label, Body/Small/Medium amount, a Neutral/Base share adding up to 100%) |
| Hero | `type="hero" · theme · color · footer` | Brand Pale by default with neutral marks and an On-Color Solid trend badge; theme="solid" (color neutral) is the dark widget: Inverse content, a Button appearance="overlay" level="inverse" in the footer |
| Motion | `MetricCard animate` | The line wipes in, bars rise, segments grow (the chart family's timing); reduced motion fades; animate={false} turns it off |

### MetricCard
Figma Metric-Card (6643:64008): a Card (Shadow, Spacing Medium) holding a Metric and a ⋮ Sub-Action. Type=KPI is an XLarge Icon-Highlight Metric; the other types (see `type`) put their marks, bar or columns under a Title-Highlight one.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `ReactNode` | — | Figma Metric-Number — pass it already formatted ("$1,680.68"). Every type shows it but `comparison`, whose columns carry the numbers. |
| `theme` | `"shadow" \| "flat" \| "pale" \| "border" \| "on-container" \| "solid" \| "semi-pale"` | — | Card theme (Figma Metric-Card uses Shadow; Type=Hero a Brand Pale fill: theme="pale" color="brand" by default). |
| `color` | `"neutral" \| "brand" \| "cyan" \| "violet" \| "green" \| "yellow" \| "orange" \| "blue" \| "purple"` | — | Card Color (Figma Card Color, for theme="pale" or "solid"): the Card's hue. Solid Neutral is the dark widget; see Card. |
| `subAction` | `CardSubAction \| ReactNode` | — | Card Sub-Action (Figma: ⋮ Button/Icon-Flat). |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` | — | Forwarded to the Card's root `<div>` (not to the Metric inside it). |
| `type` | `"kpi" \| "sparkline" \| "spark-bars" \| "goal-progress" \| "comparison" \| "category-bar" \| "hero"` | `"kpi"` | Figma Metric-Card Type (6643:64008). `kpi` (default, 6643:64007): an Icon-Highlight Metric, as before. Every other type draws a Title-Highlight Metric (no Dock-Icon unless `icon` is set) over its own content, Spacing/Gap/Medium apart (Figma Metric-Body): `sparkline` (15480:89548, Large) a trend line from `series`; `spark-bars` (15480:89594, Large) bars from `series`, the last one current; `goal-progress` (15481:1803, Large) a stacked ProgressBar from `goal`; `comparison` (15481:1848) the `label` as a Heading/Subheading title over the `comparison` columns; `category-bar` (15481:1957, Large) a bar of shares from `categories` and a row per category; `hero` (15481:2047, XLarge) a neutral trend line from `series` on a Brand Pale card (theme="solid" for the dark widget), with `footer` for its button. |

### Types
Object shapes the props above refer to.

```ts
interface CardSubAction { label: string; icon?: IconName | ReactElement; onClick?: () => void; }
type DockIconTheme = (typeof dockIconThemes)[number]
interface MetricGoal { value: number; target: number; label?: ReactNode; valueLabel?: ReactNode; }
type MetricTrendDirection = "positive" | "negative" | "normal"
```

## ✅ Do
- Format the value with units and separators (harness: metric/formatted-value).
- Give a typed MetricCard the data its type draws: series, goal, comparison or categories (harness: metric/type-data).
- Pass categories largest first and keep them to 2–7 (harness: metric/category-count).
- Pass format so the series summary, the goal's label and the category amounts read like the number ("$105.7K", "1,284 h").
- Always say what the trend compares against ("vs. last month").
- Use the same size for metrics in one row; one hero metric at most.
- Pair a worrying trend with guidance (Inline Message) or a link to details.
- Colour-code metrics by category with the Dock-Icon theme (Revenue green, Users blue…) and keep that mapping across the product.
- Use a Solid Dock-Icon only for the one metric that should lead (a goal, or an error that needs action).

## ❌ Don't
- Don't colour the number itself to show good/bad — the trend badge carries it.
- Don't show more than ~4 KPI cards in a row; group or prioritise.
- Don't round away meaningful precision in finance values.
- Don't give every tile a different colour for decoration, or rely on the icon colour alone for good/bad; the trend badge carries the status.

## Accessibility
- The trend badge has text (not colour alone); icons are decorative.
- A sparkline or spark bars is one image (role="img") named by a summary of the series (or seriesLabel); the category bar is decorative and its rows say every amount and share; goal-progress is a named progressbar.

## Content
- Labels are nouns ("Revenue"); trends read "+12% vs. last month".

## Harness (`npm run usage:check`)
| Rule | Severity | Checks | Suppress with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `card/color-ignored` | warn | Card color is the Figma Color of theme="pale" (nine hues) and theme="solid"; Shadow, Flat, Border and On-Container have no Color and ignore it. | `zen-allow-card-color: <reason>` |
| `card/solid-color` | error | Figma draws Theme=Solid in Neutral, Brand, Cyan, Yellow and Orange only; other hues render as Solid Neutral (they would fail contrast). | `zen-allow-card-color: <reason>` |
| `metric/formatted-value` | warn | Metric values are passed pre-formatted with units and separators ("$1,680.68", "2.1%"), never a raw number. | `zen-allow-metric-format: <reason>` |
| `metric/type-data` | error | A typed MetricCard gets the data its type draws (sparkline, spark-bars, hero → series; goal-progress → goal; comparison → comparison; category-bar → categories), and no data another type draws. | `zen-allow-metric-type-data: <reason>` |
| `metric/category-count` | warn | A category-bar MetricCard splits its total into 2–7 parts (the chart palette's seven colours); fold the smallest into an "Other" part. | `zen-allow-metric-categories: <reason>` |
| `api/overrides-studio-only` | error | `overrides` (Figma instance overrides of the layers a component draws itself: `{ "Sub-Action": { level: "danger" } }`) is written by Zen Studio on the pages it makes; hand-written code sets the component's own props or composes the parts (the user's call, 2026-10-10). | `zen-allow-overrides: <reason>` |
| `icon/unknown-name` | error | Icon names must exist (1,598 names that follow the Figma layer path, e.g. icon-search-medium-line); search them instead of guessing (MCP search_icons, or the Iconography page). | `zen-allow-icon-name: <reason>` |
| `interaction/no-noop-handler` | warn | Every interaction a Zen control offers works: no no-op handlers (`() => {}`, `() => undefined`), which leave a field that ignores typing and ↑/↓ or a Dismiss that stays. Chat has chat/no-locked-interaction. | `zen-allow-noop-handler: <reason>` |
| `interaction/action-without-handler` | warn | Screens, examples and templates (apps too since 2026-10-07; component source is skipped): every action does something when pressed. Flags a `Button` or `<button>` without onClick / href / type="submit" (IconButton: icon-button/needs-action), an action object ({ icon, label }) in leading, trailing, action, primaryAction, secondaryAction, subAction or actions without onClick, and pressable items whose list has no onSelect / onNavigate / onItemClick / onValueChange. Documented defaults pass: Dialog, ModalForm, SidePanel and BottomSheet actions close the overlay; a Menu opens from its trigger. Apps are not judged. | `zen-allow-action-handler: <reason>` |
